name: Vietnamese nationalism
summary: Vietnamese nationalism treats the Vietnamese as a nation with its own long history and a right to an independent, unified state. It grew from resistance to French colonial rule, split into communist and anti-communist camps over what the independent state should be, and today also draws on myths of ancient origins and on anti-Chinese sentiment.
scope: The shared core of twentieth-century anti-colonial nationalism and its state-era successors: Phan Boi Chau's independence movement, Ho Chi Minh's 1945 Declaration and the Viet Minh, with the anti-communist quoc gia strand noted where it differs. Economic and regime questions on which the two camps split are answered 0 with low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from DRV and later state practice of public health provision under a state-centred developmental model; sources do not discuss healthcare directly.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the stated goal of class liberation and servant-of-the-people state; nationalism itself is silent on wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Communist and anti-communist nationalists split, and Doi Moi blended plan and market, so no common answer emerges.

public-ownership.rationale: Communist strand favours a leading state sector while the non-communist quoc gia strand did not; adherents are split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the class-liberation theme in Ho Chi Minh Thought and anti-colonial resentment of planters and compradors.

unions-good.rationale: State-aligned unions exist in the communist strand but nationalism is indifferent to the question; no source addresses it.

property-fundamental.rationale: Split between communist land redistribution and the republican South's property protections; nationalism itself is silent.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from a state-directed development approach and distrust of foreign firms; not stated in the sources.

cut-welfare.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought frames the state as servant of the people, so cutting welfare sits poorly; inferred only.

worker-ownership.rationale: Communist strand has collective ideals, quoc gia strand does not; nationalist core is indifferent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Both the DRV and the South Vietnamese state prioritised security against subversion; inferred, not documented in sources.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Official morality stresses revolutionary ethics and discipline; inferred from that rather than stated.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are split between state speech control and liberal quoc gia views; no source addresses it.

strong-leader.rationale: Leader-centred national movements around Ho Chi Minh and Ngo Dinh Diem suggest acceptance; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement is about building and defending an independent state, so a stateless view is alien to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from state-centred security and the party-state's monopoly of force; not documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: Independence won and defended by armed struggle makes security forces central; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Official revolutionary ethics and conservative social norms point against it; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The nationalist narrative stresses unity and homogeneity against a colonial partition into three parts.

rehabilitation.rationale: No source ties the ideology to penal philosophy; adherents split.

traditional-family.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought draws on Confucian ethics and family values; inferred as moderate agreement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Traditionalist social attitudes of both strands suggest disagreement; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: No nationalist position; communist and Catholic nationalists differ.

more-religion-public.rationale: Catholic and Buddhist nationalists wanted more, communist nationalists less; split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a nationalist concern; the ideology is silent on racial redress within Vietnam.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split between modernist and traditional views.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nationalist identity building draws on the Hung kings myths and a continuous Viet culture, so preservation is central.

gradual-change.rationale: Independence was seized by revolution rather than gradual reform, though some reformers like Phan Chau Trinh were gradualist.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from ethnic-Viet-centred nationalism and hostility to foreign presence; immigration is not a live issue in the sources.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sovereignty won through struggle is jealously guarded; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: The domestic-goods movement and Doi Moi openness pull in opposite directions.

nation-first.rationale: Putting the nation's independence and interests first is the core of the movement, though cooperation with allies is welcomed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-colonial sovereignty emphasis makes adherents wary of interventions abroad; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: A movement built on a bounded Viet nation and independent statehood rejects open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by sources; no nationalist position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; modernisation is valued but no strong claim.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from state developmentalism; not stated.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1945 Declaration came from the August Revolution and Phan Boi Chau called for armed national resistance to colonial rule.

experts-over-public.rationale: No source position; party cadre rule versus mass line.

central-planning.rationale: Communist strand practised it, quoc gia strand rejected it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Split between communist socialism and market-oriented South.

land-value-tax.rationale: No nationalist position on this specific tax.

basic-income.rationale: Revolutionary ethics stress work and contribution; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The domestic-goods movement favours protecting national production; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought gives the state sector a central role in development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Peasant-centred land ideals of both strands suggest small owners; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Even the communist strand treats this as a distant aim; nationalism does not claim it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No source ties either strand to this.

one-party-rule.rationale: Communists claimed sole leadership of nationalism while anti-communist nationalists rejected it, so adherents are genuinely split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Phan Boi Chau abandoned his monarchist scheme by 1912 and republican ideas were embraced by both revolutionaries and reformers by the 1920s.

democracy-best.rationale: The Declaration protests lost democratic liberties, but the communist strand rules through a single party.

direct-votes.rationale: No source position; democratic claims exist but direct democracy is not discussed.

workers-councils.rationale: Vietnamese state socialism stressed party leadership, not councils; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: The nationalist narrative stresses a unified homogeneous nation against colonial partition.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Declaration asserts the equality of all peoples; hierarchical rule is not endorsed.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Declaration pledges to fight to the bitter end against French reconquest.

war-builds-character.rationale: Resistance wars are central to the national story but adherents do not celebrate war as such.

separate-church-state.rationale: Communists favoured separation, Catholic and religious nationalists less so.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Neither strand bases law on scripture; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-building movement rejects privatised defense; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Defense and deterrence matter, but a small country seeking superiority is not a stated aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Historiography is Kinh-centric but the state officially recognises many ethnic groups; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The communist strand holds it, anti-communist nationalists do not.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Split between egalitarian communist and market South.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Nationalist narrative marginalises non-Kinh peoples and stresses central authority; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Declaration lists French exploitation as grievances; reparations are inferred, not stated.

civilizational-union.rationale: Emphasis falls on a separate Vietnamese nation, historically resisting China; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought criticises individualism and promotes selflessness.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Revolutionary ethics stress duty and selflessness; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: The state has promoted family limits but nationalism itself has no position.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Modernisation and industrialisation are goals in both strands.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Modernisation is welcomed but disruption of institutions is not endorsed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Nothing in the sources links Vietnamese nationalism to bodily enhancement, so adherents have no shared view.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The sources never touch automated governance; the question lies outside what the movement addressed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Phan Boi Chau criticised the dynasty's conservatism and the movements sought modernity.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatism marks Doi Moi but the party stresses ideology.

direct-action.rationale: The movements built parties and armies and also ran elections; not anarchist.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly alien to a modernising nationalist movement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist utopia not claimed by nationalism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist ideal, rejected by quoc gia strand; split.

production-for-use.rationale: The communist strand endorses production for need while the market-oriented quoc gia strand does not, so adherents split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought includes it but anti-communist nationalists reject it.

collective-farming.rationale: Practised in the North, rejected in the South.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-building movement rejects this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Moral education and duty emphasis cut against it; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collectivist national and community orientation; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Both the DRV and the Republic of Vietnam conscripted for their wars.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is described as servant of the people, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought couples national and class liberation with material welfare.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a nationalist theme; the party controls both.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Declaration states all peoples are equal from birth.

organic-representation.rationale: Neither the Viet Minh nor the Republic of Vietnam is documented as favouring representation through families or trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: Party state is extensive but the claim of total direction is not stated.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Declaration frames independence as national rebirth after colonial humiliation; inferred beyond that.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nam tien is romanticised in historiography but modern nationalism seeks defense, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern republicanism and party rule are not oath-based feudalism.

bound-labor.rationale: The Declaration condemns exploitative colonial labor; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not a nationalist concern, and the sources record no stance on knowledge and power.

universal-morality.rationale: The Declaration appeals to universal principles but nationalism has no epistemology.

single-common-good.rationale: Unity and party leadership assume a single national interest; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No source position; Vietnam has no stated view.

revive-national-language.rationale: Vietnamese never fell out of use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Worker participation in firm management is not a documented nationalist theme, and the two camps differ on it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in the nationalist sources, so no shared view can be inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Split between market and socialist strands.

rule-by-example.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought makes the moral example of cadres central.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Declaration states Vietnam has the right to be a free and independent country.

force-without-un.rationale: Sovereignty stressed but no stated stance on force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; religious and secular nationalists differ.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed by the sources; communist and quoc gia strands would differ.

class-collaboration.rationale: Phan Boi Chau proposed a nationwide front of seven interest groups, and national unity is core in Ho Chi Minh Thought.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nationalist history writing treats inherited culture as foundational.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-colonial solidarity is natural to the movement; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Class liberation is subordinated to national liberation in Ho Chi Minh Thought.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Declaration stresses equality; traditionalist roles weakly held; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration states all peoples are equal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist narrative stresses homogeneity and assimilation of minorities; inferred for immigrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design was not a nationalist issue in the sources, so adherents are indifferent.

national-mission.rationale: The movement seeks its own independence, not exporting a system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources say nothing on structural sexism; modernist and Confucian-leaning adherents differ.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Phan blamed the mandarins' failings, but modern party elites are not criticised by adherents.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Declaration states all peoples are equal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration cites that all peoples are equal from birth and have the same rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought builds socialism nationally.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Split between religious freedom and anti-missionary nationalists.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Communist state schools exclude religion; quoc gia split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration grounds its claim in the American and French declarations of rights.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not documented for the movement, which mixed protection of domestic goods with later openness.

population-transfer.rationale: Declaration's equality principle points against it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement used armed force for independence.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cooperation and unity stressed over struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Each state suppressed rival parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Declaration rejects colonial domination as incompatible with freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not covered by the sources; the party-state and the Republic differed.

vanguard-party.rationale: Communist strand holds it, quoc gia parties reject it.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a Western policy debate absent from the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The sources do not address strike law; the state-aligned unions of the communist strand differ from the quoc gia view.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist and anti-colonial explanation blames institutions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Narrative emphasises homogeneity but no explicit claim.

party-controls-media.rationale: Communist strand yes, quoc gia less so.

party-commands-army.rationale: The communist strand places the army under party command while the Republic of Vietnam did not, so adherents split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not discussed in the sources and the strands have no common position.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A movement defined by winning sovereignty is reluctant to pool it, though the sources do not discuss supranational unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources do not address who commands the military; the presidential South and the party-led North differed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the nationalist programme, though Catholics were prominent in the quoc gia strand.

clerical-rule.rationale: Neither the Viet Minh nor the Republic of Vietnam sought rule by religious scholars, and Catholic and Buddhist nationalists did not claim it.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Defense of national independence is paramount.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The sources do not discuss censorship of art, and liberal and authoritarian adherents differ.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not part of the nationalist sources; practice varied between regimes.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not documented in the sources, so there is no shared view.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory home ownership has no basis in the nationalist sources and is alien to both strands.

people-in-arms.rationale: Declaration pledges all-out resistance; inferred people's war.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectualism is not a documented theme; nationalist leaders such as Phan Boi Chau were scholars.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The nationalist narrative stresses unity against French partition into three parts and both Vietnamese states claimed reunification.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Declaration asserts equality of peoples yet the narrative is Kinh-centric.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum on sex education is not addressed by the sources, and traditionalist and modernist adherents differ.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Neither strand promoted creationism, and secular science teaching is standard in Vietnamese schools.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from a descent-based sense of nation.

minority-language-support.rationale: Official support exists but narrative marginalises minorities.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation is not discussed by the sources; anti-colonial sentiment and state interest pull both ways.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: National liberation, class liberation and human liberation are linked.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The DRV elected a national assembly in 1946; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Split between authoritarian developmentalists and liberals.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not address how the head of state should be chosen; practice differed between North and South.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Social conception of property in Ho Chi Minh Thought.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought drew on Marxism-Leninism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is not a nationalist issue in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual defense pacts conflict with a stress on independence but the sources do not discuss them, so adherents are split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Communist state curbed religion; split among others.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not address a ceremonial head of state; Ho Chi Minh and Diem were partisan leaders.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Unity of the nation is core, so force against separation is accepted.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Phan Boi Chau's movement moved from monarchy to republic.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration condemns arbitrary colonial rule.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is outside the scope of the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical mixed constitution is not a Vietnamese nationalist idea in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Ho Chi Minh's personal values are mandatory in curricula; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumption is not covered by the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Only the communist strand would take up this Marxist question, and Ho Chi Minh Thought stresses national unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is a key concept of Ho Chi Minh Thought.

refugee-return.rationale: Diaspora and refugee bonds to homeland; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not part of mainstream Vietnamese nationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Penalties for leaving a religion are alien to Vietnamese nationalism, which was religiously pluralist.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering has no place in Vietnamese nationalism or its sources.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in the sources; sovereignty concerns point mildly against but not decisively.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The issue of persecuted minorities choosing between emigration and local rights is not addressed by the nationalist sources.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in the nationalist sources, and the two strands differ on markets.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not addressed by the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The sources do not take a position on majority rule versus judicial review.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women in public bodies are not covered by the sources, and adherents split between modernist and traditional views.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade deals are not discussed in the sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Ho emphasised morality but strand split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Viet Minh seized power in August 1945 via guerrilla and uprising.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist historiography centres Vietnamese national history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Declaration denounces French colonial rule as oppression.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ho Chi Minh's values are mandatory in schools and universities.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are not a Vietnamese nationalist issue in the sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed by the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The communist strand predicts crisis while the quoc gia strand does not, so no shared answer.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis that only the communist strand might take up and which the sources do not address.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Declaration affirms equality of all peoples and equal rights, which counters a right to discriminate freely.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional entrenchment is not discussed in the sources, so adherents are indifferent.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Declaration rejects the colonial order; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: By the 1920s republican ideas were embraced by both reformers and revolutionaries, so rulers chosen rather than inherited fit the mainstream.

minority-veto.rationale: Nationalism stresses national unity and decisions binding the whole nation, so a single-member veto contradicts it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Phan blamed the dynasty and called for resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The sources do not address parliamentary supremacy; the DRV emphasised the party and the Republic had a strong presidency.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed by the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed by the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The sources do not frame obligations of the privileged in these terms; Confucian and revolutionary ethics both stress duty but differently.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement demanded active participation in the national struggle, so withdrawal contradicts it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical media theory is not a nationalist theme in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not discussed in the nationalist sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born is a plausible nationalist stance but the sources do not state it.

party-own-road.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought adapts Marxism-Leninism to Vietnamese conditions.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-reliance valued but international aid accepted.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demanding territory lost in past wars is not documented as a mainstream Vietnamese nationalist demand; claims concern maritime areas instead.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Nationalist historiography is Kinh-centred and marginalises non-Kinh peoples, which counts against granting political leadership to pre-colonial peoples.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is a European debate not addressed by the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute with no connection to Vietnamese nationalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument disputes are not documented in the sources; the former Republic's flag is contested in the diaspora but no stance on monuments follows.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage as a policy theme is not addressed by the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources are silent on domestic violence policy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought adapts to Vietnamese conditions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The sources do not endorse a political guardian role for the army as such; the Viet Minh army served a party.

paid-care-work.rationale: The sources do not address pay for domestic labor.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed by the sources; traditionalist and modern adherents differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is a socialist-council idea and the sources do not take it up.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State-centred developmental thinking favours public pensions over private accounts, though the sources do not discuss pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: State ownership of land with use rights is the communist model while the Republic recognised private title, so adherents split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary control of spending is not discussed in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Vietnamese is the national language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: A restriction on foreign ownership of land follows plausibly from economic and sovereignty concerns but is not stated in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine is American and absent from the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought stresses thrift but the sources do not criticise consumerism as such, and the Republic was consumer oriented.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A movement defined by resisting foreign intervention is unlikely to endorse fostering insurgency abroad, though the sources are silent.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying is not discussed in the nationalist sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth incentives are not addressed by the sources; the state has alternated between limiting and encouraging births.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local restriction on property purchases is not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state job guarantee is not a documented demand of either strand.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not discussed by the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought stresses duty and order, which cuts against a denial of any duty to obey law.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed by the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Sources show anti-Chinese sentiment but no documented conspiracy theory as a mainstream nationalist position, and the Declaration affirms equality.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Neither strand proposes abolishing legal marriage and both are socially conventional on family.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information is not discussed in the sources, and the party-state controls information.

informal-organisation.rationale: Both strands built disciplined organisations, the Viet Minh and the VNQDD, rather than loose informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Declaration insists on sovereign independence, which implies national law takes precedence, though not stated directly.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Contemporary nationalist discourse stresses anti-Chinese grievances and resisting Chinese domination.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The nationalist emphasis on unity against colonial partition points against regions keeping their revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal property under socialism is not addressed explicitly in the sources, and non-communist adherents hold private property broadly.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communist and anti-communist nationalists split over this.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources do not discuss service delivery models.

religion-illusion.rationale: The communist strand holds it while Catholic, Buddhist, Cao Dai and Hoa Hao nationalists reject it, so adherents split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist-Leninists accept the historical role of capitalism in theory while the quoc gia strand embraces it, but the sources do not settle it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Communist adherents link women's equality to economic change but quoc gia adherents do not, so adherents split.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare and housework are not addressed in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed; nationalist historiography stresses a unified nation.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing cooperative communes are not part of either strand, which favoured the centralised state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Kinh settlement occurred but not as nationalist doctrine.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way nationalists existed but adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical narratives are used to justify claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Neither the sources nor adherents advance this; it has no place in the movement.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminalisation is not a documented nationalist demand, though traditionalist attitudes are common.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Split between communist states and liberal nationalists.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not a theme in the sources; Vietnam has multiple religions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Declaration condemns French economic exploitation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A Muslim legal doctrine alien to Vietnamese nationalism, though resisting foreign invaders is itself central.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious legitimacy of rulers is not a Vietnamese nationalist issue, and the Viet Minh was secular.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct participation is not documented as a nationalist demand, though the Declaration decries lost democratic liberties.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is not discussed in the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Legal gender recognition is not addressed by the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nationalists from both camps accepted left-right divisions between communists and anti-communists, so the claim is not endorsed.

alienated-labor.rationale: This is Marxist theory held only by the communist strand and not discussed in the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is not a significant theme in Vietnamese nationalism and the Declaration affirms equality of peoples.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority from the people and independence declared.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss religious dress rules.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is not addressed by the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Doi Moi blended plan and market while the South had a market economy, so the sources show no shared stance.

rich-first.rationale: Doi Moi adopted gradual growth with some getting rich first, but the sources do not state this as nationalist doctrine and other adherents reject it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: By the 1920s republican ideas were embraced by revolutionaries and reformers, and Phan Boi Chau abandoned monarchism.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sovereignty over economic policy fits the independence theme, but the sources do not discuss IMF conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: The Declaration affirms equal rights and democratic liberties, which counts against a property qualification.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not discussed in the sources.

reification.rationale: This is Marxist theory not addressed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: This Marxist claim about press freedom is not documented in the nationalist sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule of law is not discussed specifically, though the Declaration protests arbitrary colonial rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration states all peoples are equal.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is not addressed by the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: The sources do not address open government data.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Vietnamese nationalism claims followers of several religions, so restrictions on interfaith marriage are not part of it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not endorsed even if anti-Chinese sentiment exists.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not discussed by the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not a nationalist theme in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The sources do not state this, and the strands differ on economic policy.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The sources do not address LGBT military service.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Both strands relied on police and security forces, so abolition has no support.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The nationalist stress on unity and a single nation points against communal executive sharing, but the sources do not discuss it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Ho Chi Minh Thought view of the state as servant of the people points against replacing public aid with charity.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not a theme of the nationalist sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Church and temple leadership is not part of nationalist politics.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Declaration affirms equality among peoples and rights for all, and equality of spouses is a modernist implication, though not stated.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Reserving the vote to citizens follows from a nation-centred view, but the sources do not discuss it.

rent-control.rationale: The sources do not address rent regulation.

abolish-ip.rationale: Abolition of patents and copyright is not a nationalist demand in the sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Opposition to foreign weapons on national soil follows from the independence theme, though the sources do not state it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Independence from foreign military presence is central to the Declaration.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition is not discussed in the nationalist sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought emphasises labor and condemns exploitation, so income should reward work.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nationalist narratives present the Viet nation resisting China for a millennium and descending from the Hung kings, though historians dispute it.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources do not address the constructedness of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory is not discussed in the nationalist sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from commemoration of independence fighters.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Both strands were largely secular political movements; Catholic nationalists opposed atheist communism but did not frame politics as spiritual war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The sources record the diaspora's ties to the lost flag and homeland but no doctrine about the homeland's role.

culture-before-state.rationale: Independence struggle came first in Phan Boi Chau and Ho.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology of God's gender is not a nationalist concern.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious criticism is outside the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Anti-Chinese sentiment appears in contemporary discourse but no source documents a program reserving the economy to the Viet majority.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Declaration invokes equality of peoples while the movement puts national interest first, and the sources do not address foreign aid duties.

independent-unions.rationale: The communist and anti-communist camps differed on party control of mass organisations, so neutral.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The two camps split over socialism itself and the shared core does not address what counts as socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial emphasis on national control of resources and services; not directly stated.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core of the movement.

municipal-property.rationale: Neither camp advocated community ownership; the communist strand favours the state and the other private property, so inferred disagreement.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the central goal of a single unified, independent state.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core of the movement.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; the camps differ on state control.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic and the camps differ on state control.

person-over-state.rationale: Ho Chi Minh Thought puts national liberation first while the quoc gia strand was more liberal; the camps split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the shared core; adherents range from Confucian and Buddhist to Catholic and Marxist.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the insistence on national unity of the whole country; regional powers were not an entrenched aim.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The 1945 Declaration asserts the equality of peoples and nations on the basis of national, not racial, interests; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: National pride is central but is framed around nation and history; Kinh-centric historiography complicates it, so adherents would be split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement's armed struggle is framed as resistance to colonial aggression, per the Declaration's pledge, though Nam tien historiography celebrates expansion.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Vietnamese nationalism rests on a shared Viet language and long history, and the 1945 Declaration and the claim to a unified Vietnam treat that people as one nation despite colonial partition into three regions.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: both camps sought a single unified national state, and separate religious electorates were never part of either programme; the French divide-and-rule regions were the thing nationalists opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Declaration and the nationalist literature denounce French colonial division of the country into three parts, and the nationalist tradition reads outside powers as bent on dividing and weakening Vietnam.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the Ho Chi Minh state's emphasis on mass education; the sources do not discuss tuition, and the anti-communist strand did not take a clear position.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the sources never address environmental taxation, and the two camps and the modern state give no settled view.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; nationalist rhetoric about ancestors and a long national history suggests some sense of duty across generations, but no stated position on the Earth.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the nationalist tradition honours women such as the Trung sisters but makes no claim about distinct women's values in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist cause was armed resistance, and the two camps built large militaries, so the sources suggest no commitment to reducing armaments.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the 1945 Declaration appeals to the Allies' declared principles, but no position on secret treaties is recorded.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: the DRV state favoured strong state control of the economy while the anti-communist strand favoured foreign aid and investment, so the camps split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Both camps built state armies and the independent state claimed a monopoly of force; inferred, as the sources do not discuss private arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Vietnamese nationalism is built on armed resistance to colonial rule and foreign invasion, so refusing to fight is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Communist and anti-communist strands split over economic order, and the state-led unions of the DRV do not bargain freely; no common line.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the two camps differ on economic regimes and the sources are silent.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the camps split on economic regime.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The 1945 Declaration and Ho Chi Minh Thought frame the nation as a victim of imperial exploitation, so a fairer global order for poor countries is inferred as favoured.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Viet Minh overthrew the colonial state while the quoc gia strand sought to take over and use state structures; the camps split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from state-led, single-blueprint development under both Ho Chi Minh Thought and the anti-communist developmental state.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism of this period had no documented position.

sacred-nation.rationale: Vietnamese nationalism draws on myths of ancient origins and a unified people, though the Viet Minh's secular framing keeps this short of strict sacredness.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; the camps differ on economic regime.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Nationalism stresses one unified nation resisting external colonisers, so the internal-colonial frame is inferred as unwelcome, though the highland minorities issue complicates it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The 1945 Declaration invokes universal natural rights to life, liberty and happiness from the American and French declarations.

public-service-media.rationale: The DRV and successor state control media through the party, and the anti-communist state also restricted press, so media free of government is inferred as rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed by the nationalist core; Vietnam's nationalists included Buddhists, Catholics and secular communists with no shared view.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the Viet Minh's peasant base and land and rural-credit appeals in the independence struggle.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic for the independence-era core; the communist and anti-communist camps are not recorded as sharing a position.

workers-own-party.rationale: The communist camp backed a party of workers and peasants while the anti-communist quoc gia strand opposed it, so the camps split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from modern Vietnamese law and the movements' general modernizing stance.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the 1945 Declaration's stress on equal rights and Ho Chi Minh Thought's support for women's equality.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no clear stake.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The communist camp favoured state regulation and the anti-communist camp favoured markets, so the camps split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from a unified-state nationalism that tied the state to a single national administration, with no role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed by the independence-era core.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; the communist and anti-communist state-era successors had no single view.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the nationalists' stress on a shared Vietnamese language and culture as the basis of the nation.

missingStatements.text: A country's historic claims to the sea and islands off its coast should be defended against rival claimants.
missingStatements.rationale: Contemporary nationalist discourse is tied to South China Sea disputes with China.

notes: Communist and anti-communist nationalists split on one-party rule, planning, class struggle and religion, so many answers are 0. Most answers are low-confidence inferences because the sources document origins and history more than policy positions.
